title: api-robustness-standardize-retry-after-idempotency-consistent-error-codes-openai-compat
author: Ava Thompson
description:
Motivation:
OpenAI-compatible clients expect consistent rate limit semantics (HTTP 429 with Retry-After header), deterministic idempotency handling for POST endpoints (create/complete/generate), and a small set of stable error codes for programmatic retries. We observed several customer bug reports where streaming requests would receive inconsistent error shapes (some missing retry-after), idempotency keys were accepted but not reflected in the canonical response, and the openai-compat layer returned mixed internal error messages that prevented standard SDK retries.

This PR standardizes rate-limit semantics across streaming and non-streaming endpoints, enforces strict idempotency key behavior for create/completions/generate endpoints, and maps internal error variants to a small canonical set of OpenAI-compatible error codes. It also includes compatibility shims for structured output and tool-calling flows to preserve idempotency and retry semantics during partial/streamed responses.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist):
- [x] Return HTTP 429 with Retry-After header consistently for all rate-limited paths (api gateway + runtime).
- [x] Add deterministic idempotency key reconciliation (store canonical request fingerprint, return existing response metadata when duplicate).
- [x] Ensure streaming responses surface Retry-After as initial control frame when possible and as trailing metadata when stream already started.
- [x] Canonicalize error responses: map internal errors to {"type": "rate_limit" | "invalid_request" | "server_error" | "auth_error" | "timeout"}.
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat layer docs and tests to assert compatibility behavior.
- [x] Add integration tests covering retries for streaming tool-calls and structured output.

Detailed changes:
- API gateway middleware: added RateLimitMiddleware that sets 429 + Retry-After (seconds) and a machine-readable header X-RateLimit-Reset iso8601 when available. Previously some internal paths returned 503 or 429 without Retry-After.
- Idempotency service: new IdempotencyStore interface (in-memory impl for tests, Dynamo/Redis-backed in production) with reconciler that computes a canonical fingerprint of the request body + route + model + function-call shape. If a duplicate with a terminal response exists, return that response metadata (status, location, response-id) instead of re-executing.
- Streaming protocol: when a streaming response is rejected for rate-limit, we now send a control frame JSON: {"error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":...,"retry_after": <seconds>}} as the first chunk; if the stream already started, we append a final control metadata message. This preserves client streaming parsers.
- Error mapping: centralized ErrorMapper component that converts various internal exceptions to the OpenAI-compatible envelope. Errors include code, type, message, and optional param. This replaces ad-hoc error shapes in the openai-compat layer.
- Tool/Function-calling: ensure idempotency metadata is associated with tool-invocation results. If an in-flight tool call is duplicated, return the canonical result and mark events in audit log.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for middleware, idempotency reconciler, and error mapper added.
- Integration tests simulate concurrent duplicate requests with identical idempotency keys and assert only one execution and consistent response.
- Streaming integration tests emulate half-open streams and assert Retry-After frames are present.
- Backwards compatibility: behaviour is additive; existing clients receive 429 where appropriate and structured error envelopes. The openai-compat shim keeps legacy message fields for a deprecation period.

Notes:
- Linear tickets ENG-4621 tracked flaky retries in streaming endpoints; ENG-4689 consolidated idempotency design. SUP-1082 is the customer report that triggered the hotfix.
- Follow-up work: metrics for idempotency hit/miss ratio and dashboards for Retry-After frequency (SLO impact).

release_notes: Standardize 429 Retry-After semantics across streaming and non-streaming endpoints; deterministic idempotency reconciliation for create/generate endpoints; canonical OpenAI-compatible error envelopes; improved compatibility for streaming tool-calls and structured output.
